questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Choosing a destination where I spoke the language and I was interested in the units

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: So easy, Deakin has been really good at communicating

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Dekin offered to pick you up at the airport, hosted an introductory meeting for exchange students very early, they send several introductory emails with informations about everything relevant for coming there and similarly posted most of the information in a Facebook group

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Before I left, I was quite nervous about finding accommodation. I was lucky to have some mutual friends in Melbourne, so I found accommodation through them. 
My impression is that you can easily find something through Facebook groups, Fairy Floss etc.
However, you have to just travel to Melbourne and book Airbnb for the first 1-2-3 weeks, as physically have to go out and see the apartments. It can be difficult to find a place with other australians and easier to find other nationalities or a whole apartment which you can share with other danes

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend finding accommodation off campus. Firstly, the rent in the university housing is really high (8000 thousand DKK), it is really far from Melbourne CBD (1.5 hour transport), the rooms are small, most other students there are much younger.
Of course it depends on what you want, but I think it has been really cool to live off campus and be able to use the city more. Those who have lived on campus have spent a lot of time travelling back and forth, as nothing happens out on Deakin Campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was sent an introduction to Deakin's website where you applied for the courses. It was a really easy process where you could choose when the classes were and also easily change courses if it became relevant.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Deakin both have an office for exchange students, where I could go and ask for help or write to a help-desk online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the subjects I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
In general, my experience is that the level is lower than at UCPH, I would therefore recommend to take units that you actually find exciting, as they will not be difficult.
Once you have been assigned the subjects, you can choose when you want to take the classes, which means you can be strategic and group the classes into a few days, allowing you to have long weekends with the opportunity to travel. At the same time, all the classes are recorded, making it easy to follow along

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level has been really easy. In many ways it is similar to high school with a lecturer and a seminar with interactive teaching. There is much less to read than at KU - often only 20 pages for a lecture, in contrast to political science at KU with around 60-100 pages minimum.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's very different. Some of my lectures were online, while others were physical, but there were only a maximum of 60 students per lecture. Everything is recorded, which means that very few show up

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Intro to Aboriginal Studies, Anthropology of Crime and Violence, Lobbying and Advocacy and Australia and the Indo-Pacific: Identity, interests, and order

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think the introduction to Aboriginal studies has been really interesting - it's really easy, but it's exciting to learn about the side of Australian culture and history that you don't usually hear much about.

questions.answer: A student visa to Australia is very expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I was lucky that public transport was free due to the oil crisis, but that's something to be considered.
I thought rent would be more expensive, but you can easily find something for 5000-6000 kr.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's really a lot going on on campus if you want to be a part of it - countless sports clubs, etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: everything you can think of

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I got a network outside of uni, so wasn't part of any of it unfortunately

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: As much as possible - I especially thought Uluru and Tasmania were amazing. It's easy to travel around Australia, so if you want to, I really think you should!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: So easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I think it was a bit difficult because so few people show up for classes. Unfortunately, it's easiest to have contact with other Danes, and there are so many down there, and other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing at all, it is so easy coming here and aussies are the most friendly people ever

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
there is such beautiful nature that Australians are really good at taking advantage of.
Happy hour with cheap beer!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't be afraid of not getting any friends, even though it's difficult to make contact with other Australians, there are really many Danes down here, and Danes find Danes...
2. Take advantage of your time here and say yes to as many things as possible - and vice versa, ask people if they want to go out for a beer or coffee, most people want to experience as much as possible.
3. if you can, try to seek out Australians, they are truly amazing - it's especially easy through sports clubs

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The weather is very changeable here and can get cold in their winter, but still around 10-15 degrees.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: it has all been fantastic, I can only recommend going !!! - it has been fantastic to have some other subjects with other focuses than available at KU, to create a network and a life in another country and that most people going on exchange here are mostly here to enjoy their time which creates a lovely vibe of just going with the flow !

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I've been lucky enough to live with Australians, which have introduced me to all their friends and been amazing at just bringing me along. However, it has also been nice to be able to speak danish every now and then. I've been surprised by how many other exchange students / danes that come here with friends, which make it difficult as a single person to navigate making friends and travel plans with people who already have friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
